articleTitle: Business process re-engineering; a concurrent engineering process
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Current Developments in Concurrent Engineering - Methodologies and Tools
abstract: Business process re-engineering (BPR) involves a radical rethinking and replacement of a business's key processes. This paper illustrates how businesses can implement new product introduction (NPI) processes using concurrent engineering (CE) techniques with a BPR approach, and how the scale of success can be improved compared to more cautious approaches. It contrasts the BPR approach with other improvement techniques, describes the features of BPR, and examines potential areas where BPR can be applied to CE-NPI processes. Measures for establishing how well the approach is succeeding in a particular case are also outlined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer support for cooperative teams: applications in concurrent engineering
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Current Developments in Concurrent Engineering - Methodologies and Tools
abstract: The cooperative team, a key concept in concurrent engineering, is also a symbol of large-scale organisational changes that have swept through industry in the western hemisphere in recent years. The old multi-layer hierarchies are being modified, if not abandoned, in favour of team-based organisational design. In parallel with these changes a new class of IT systems has emerged, popularly termed groupware. Based on the networked PC environment, groupware models the user as a cooperating group, not as an individual working in isolation. Recognising that the nature of workgroup cooperation will vary in different workplace scenarios, technology designers have developed a wide range of groupware tools. This paper surveys these tools and assesses their usefulness in the context of concurrent engineering methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Current Developments in Concurrent Engineering - Methodologies and Tools
abstract: The author describes ICL's approach to flexible manufacturing, set up to deal with a wide variety of electronic products simultaneously (rather than focused volume lines on a few selected products), which has allowed them to meet the demands of the new shorter timescales but only at the cost of more intensive manual effort. It has also emphasised the need to balance skilled resources in the manufacturing operations with a cheaper (hence smaller and less highly trained) workforce on the production lines. The very core of concurrent engineering-'fuzzy gates' allowing parallel activities to occur-is itself the greatest challenge to the individuals from manufacturing who are involved in the cross functional teams.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Current Developments in Concurrent Engineering - Methodologies and Tools
abstract: Whilst each application of re-engineering has achieved a measure of success in its own right, the need to continuously, and seamlessly, support such initiatives has now become widely accepted in many industries. The paper describes the problems of allowing a functionally based structure to become the dominant force in a business attempting innovative product development and new product introduction. It also outlines the ways in which Siemens Plessey has previously tackled this issue, and is now attempting to provide a basis for sustained improvement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Current Developments in Concurrent Engineering - Methodologies and Tools
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of logistics support in a product's complete life-cycle, and outlines a strategic framework for logistics support, called CALS. The effect of CALS framework on the new standards for storage, retrieval, sharing and exchange of technical information are discussed. This is followed by a review of the techniques, tools and technology needed for a product's logistics support. In particular, a method called logistics support analysis is presented to achieve this objective.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Current Developments in Concurrent Engineering - Methodologies and Tools
abstract: Increasingly organisations are required to invest in new technology to create an IT infrastructure. The question arises how to justify the infrastructure investment when the activities that generate the benefit are subject to future management decisions. If the decision has already been made then the benefits can be directly incorporated into the business justification. The goal of this paper is to draw attention to the application of option analysis, look at the impact of technical maturity on investment justification and review the position of concurrent art-to-product environments, CAPE.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
